questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted a place with interesting classes and from where I could travel and see the rest of the country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy- Leeds has a "before you arrive" guide and information sessions when you get there

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a bit of mix up with the taxi company, but the university paid for a taxi to take to me to my student accommodation upon arrival and the student accommodation office were wonderful as well

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You can live in dorms or in "shared houses" which basically is a flat

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: For shared houses it is "self catered" but for some of the dorms you could choose the catered option

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I liked living close to campus - Headingley is the student area and it has some lovely options for cafés and pubs but there is a longer way to campus (around 30 minutes on foot) - you can also rent a bike but I didn't feel comfortable biking there as the cars could be a bit crazy

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No struggles there and when I wanted to change a course I wrote the woman responsible for it at my school and she changed it immediately

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just had to choose which ones I liked online and then I was signed up for it

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get a contact person at the school you're attached to and you can write them  - the student hub and international office also has lots of opportunities and they are happy to help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted and I was allowed to change one of them 1 week in

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to check the 'isa' box when browsing for courses and ask questions if you're unsure about anything!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I'd say they are a bit easier than at UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: the classes are smaller and there are a lot more "chat with the person next to you work" which also meant that you had to prepare more than I do at home - but I liked that and I've brought it home with me. The seminar tutors are lovely and good at contextualising what you're saying

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Drama text and performance 
One about Charles Dickens and Dickens adaptation
Other voices: One about other voices in Victorian Literature

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed 'Drama: text and performance' - it is a first year course about theatre history and for assignments you had to do your own adaptation of plays discussed in classes

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to buy all the "inventar" for your accommodation and that is a lot

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cinema tickets and theatre tickets- they are wonderfully cheap!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sooo many societies available, I wanted to do the archery class but was too late for it, so look out for if it sounds like something you'd like

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of societies of all sorts. Lots of societies also arrange some sort of ball each semester so look out for those if you're interested

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I never really went but the film society had some awesome movie showings. Many socities also have a 'Give It A Go' (GIGO) in the beginning of the semester where you can try it out and see if you'd like to continue

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: 10000% go see York, it's really nice. Go see the nature around Yorkshire. I'd recommend Ilkley moor, Skipton, Grassington and the cute towns around Yorkshire. Also take the train to Edinburgh

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. I'd say there are less europeans in the UK compared to a few years ago (damn u, Brexit!!!) but so many lovely people

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies or talk to them in classes

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The small talk aspect - we are so much more direct in Denmark, and there are a lot more polite chitter chatter there before you get to the "real deal"

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved how people acknowledge each other - everyone says thanks, cheers, and sorry when you're holding the door or stuff like that

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Remember deadlines 2) Go see stuff outside Leeds too 3) Have lunch at Kirkgate market (and go check out the Corn Exchange)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to talk to your teachers. And if you're interested in literature and theatre go check out the Playhouse Lab

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I've been introduced to so many new topics I didn't knew existed and I learned a lot literature. I enjoyed the cultural and academic aspect

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was probably in the beginning of my stay, when the taxi was seriously delayed and I got to accommodation too late, but I called the security (they are on Campus 24/7) and they were extremely nice and helped me. I also had to get used to the architecture and the fact that there are a lot more trash on the street than back home- but that was culture shock and it passed rather quickly

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go, enjoy the many accents, the bad weather, and the people!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
